explanation: Greece doesn't have a single codified, widely-cited taboo against beckoning with a curled index finger the way it does for the moutza or the OK sign — it isn't named in the main Greek-gesture guides. That said, it fits the broader European pattern where a curled 'come here' finger (especially palm-up) can come across as brusque or commanding, with an open-hand, palm-down wave seen as the more polite way to call someone over.
local_tip: To call someone over politely, use an open-hand, palm-down wave rather than a single curled finger.

also_check.note: Curled-finger beckoning is considered very rude and can be seen as a challenge.
Beckoning with one finger is disrespectful; a palm-down hand wave is preferred.
Common casually, but can seem condescending in formal or professional contexts.
